---
description: Delegate this task to a rush sub-agent instead of doing it yourself
---

**Opt-in only:** run `/rush <task>` (or “delegate this to rush”) once; never auto-invoke on follow-ups unless asked again.

## When not to delegate
Refuse in one sentence and offer direct help for interactive merges/conflict resolution/design/debugging, work dependent on this chat's decisions/files/partial state, requests where the user supplied the fix (you must verify it), one- or two-line changes, or a plan being worked out with the user.

## Smart means launch and wait
`rush run --role smart` reads the repo, plans, delegates, reviews, and reports. Tell it **what and why** (goal, observable acceptance, evidence, hard scope/constraints), not how. Honor caller hard constraints and policy, including CI-only verification when requested. Launch in repo/worktree and await completion. Do not prescribe implementation plans, file:line edits, sequence, tools/roles/workers, or a verification checklist; do not forbid its internal delegation. Nested executors are expected: don't stop or ask; wait.
Only `--role`, `--session`, `--json`, and when warranted `--restrict-run`; don't tune models/effort/`--agents`. Don't coach mid-run: `sessions inject` is only for genuinely new facts or changed operator requirements. A follow-up passes reviewer findings, CI output, or new requirements verbatim into the same `--session`.

## Fallback when `rush` hits rate limits

When using Claude, an armed `/rush-fallback <agent>` means switch to that agent immediately and silently on either trigger: peak-hours refusal (match `is in peak hours (` in failed-run stderr or JSON `.error`) or hard limit (weekly/monthly account budget exhausted, suspension, or account quota exceeded without a retry-after in this session). This fallback never authorizes `--allow-peak-hours`; add that flag only when a human explicitly authorizes it in this request.

**Hard limit (all CLI targets):** exhausted weekly/monthly account quota, suspended account, or account quota exceeded with no retry-after that lands within this session. Context-capacity overflow is not account quota exhaustion or authorization to switch providers; follow the context-recovery guidance below. With no armed fallback, deny the reroute immediately: report exact error, provider, and retry/reopen time if supplied; stop and wait for human direction. Do not prompt for permission to bypass or choose a route. Claude's armed fallback is the sole automatic exception described above; other CLIs cannot arm it.
Never fallback for recoverable issues: if a timeout is reported, inspect its reported source and retry only when caller/operator-authorized and permitted by the safe-resume rules below; do not automatically increase `--timeout`. For other recoverable issues, wait/retry short 429; retry 5xx/network blips and escalate if persistent; fix bad flags/workspace/prompt. Local fallback is last resort.

## Never self-add `--allow-peak-hours`
`rush providers set <id> --peak-hours HH:MM-HH:MM` configures the provider's local-time window (overnight allowed; `--peak-hours off` clears); `--peak-hours-message "..."` sets and `--peak-hours-message ""` clears the note; both honor `--local`. `rush run --allow-peak-hours` bypasses one invocation only; no persistent equivalent. Never add it unless a human explicitly authorizes it in this request. Without armed fallback, report refusal/retry-after and wait; don't switch providers, add the flag, or rerun until the local-time window closes. Armed Claude fallback switches as specified above.

## Resuming after `exit_reason: "awaiting_answer"`
`rush run --json` may return `exit_reason: "awaiting_answer"` when its own agent calls `ask_question`; this is deliberate, not a crash/provider refusal. `.error` includes the question/options and resume guidance; `.final_text` is usually empty. Use the original role (`--role` is required) and same session only after the process actually exits; the complete question and safe resume rules are below. `STALLED` status alone is not a resume signal; it is not `exit_reason: "stalled"`.

## Orchestrator mode — and why a worker's question is NOT your problem
With `--role smart` and configured worker (`rush models use ... --worker <model>`), Rush restores the `agent` tool despite its default sub-agent ban; `agentic_fetch` remains banned. Orchestrator mode delegates hands-on edits/writes/commands in worker-context-sized chunks and treats every report as a CLAIM: independently verify actual diff/test evidence.
A configured worker overrides `--agents single` for smart; that flag only prevents delegation without a worker or outside smart. For a hard no-delegation guarantee, don't configure a worker.
Configured reviewer adds one final review turn to successful smart runs and reviews the whole session; executor text remains `final_text`, reviewer conclusion is additive in JSON `review` (empty if none). Failed/canceled/timed-out/queued runs unchanged; explicit reviewer role isn't extended; override isn't persisted. Unconfigure reviewer to disable.

**A paused child is not an exited top-level run.** A legacy `agent` child question returns a `SUB-AGENT QUESTION` result while the parent continues; resume that same child through the `agent` tool with its exact `resume_session_id` and the answer as the prompt. For a currently held batch-child question, use `inspect_agent` and its `held_question` identity; answer the existing held generation via `inject_agent(child_session_id="<full child session id>", message="<answer>")`. Do not resume/re-delegate that held batch child as a new generation, and do not inject into a child with `sessions inject`. A child `awaiting_answer` or held question never proves that the top-level run process exited.

## Launching (Claude)
Use `--role smart` for non-trivial work, `fast` for one-liners; worker roles are optional and may be reached directly or indirectly through smart orchestration; reviewer is optional. Neither role is auto-selected. The `rush models use` configuration command accepts `--worker <model>` or `--reviewer <model>` without positional arguments; example combined configuration: `rush models use <smart> <fast> --worker <model> --reviewer <model>`. Example reviewer-only run: `rush run --role reviewer --session "pr-42-review" "review this diff"`.
Use stable task-meaningful session IDs, unique across the project: linked worktrees share `<main>/.rush`, so old IDs resume. Session belongs to creating checkout; another checkout gets `belongs to <root>`; use `rush sessions fork <id> --cwd <path>` to continue there.
No explicit `--timeout` by default (`0`); the default six-hour total wall-clock cap still applies, including active work and waits (see **Time limits** below). `--idle-timeout` defaults 15m. Don't add an arbitrary `--timeout`.
When using Claude `Bash` `run_in_background: true`, redirect output/error to `.rush/stdin/<task>.out` and `.err`. Launch one run at a time; retain its physical process handle and wait for its completion notification, then inspect that run and its diff. A process completion does not prove its related batch work is terminal. Never sleep-poll or launch a duplicate into live/unknown work. Integration, staging, commits, and worktree cleanup belong to the invoking parent and require explicit authorization plus confirmed process and related-batch termination. Bash command must be bare `rush run ...`; never append `&`/wrapper (false completion causes duplicate locked-session launches). One command per call:
```
Bash({ command: "rush run --role smart --session foo --json < .rush/stdin/foo.prompt > .rush/stdin/foo.out 2> .rush/stdin/foo.err", run_in_background: true })
```
Write multiline prompt to `.rush/stdin/<task>.prompt`, feed `< file`; avoid multiline positional quotes. Rush permissions are auto-approved: use only workspaces you can lose; consider `--restrict-run`.
Default one run per worktree. Parallelize only for independent file sets when user asks or task requires fan-out. Every prompt must name its scope and siblings/scopes, forbid touching other scopes, and forbid git writes (`commit`, `add`, `stash`, `reset`, `checkout`/`restore`, `rebase`, `merge`); read-only `status`/`diff`/`log` okay. Orchestrator stages/commits sequentially after verifying diffs. Use separate worktrees for overlapping edits. Tests must stay within assigned packages (e.g. `go test ./internal/foo/...`, never `./...`) or be skipped and reported; run shared suite once after merge. Honor caller CI-only policy and do not claim local checks ran.

## Scoping permissions for a delegation — `--restrict-run`
Permissions auto-approve by default. For untrusted/exploratory prompts or overly broad workspaces, use deny-by-default:
```
rush run --restrict-run --role fast --allow-tool view --allow-bash 'git diff' --allow-bash 'glob:go *' --session "ci-123" "summarize the diff"
```
`--allow-tool <name>` repeats for non-bash tools or `tool:action` (e.g. `view`, `edit:write`); `bash`/`bash:execute` are no-ops. `--allow-bash '<pattern>'` repeats: word-boundary prefix (`git diff` matches `git diff HEAD~1`, not `git difftool`), `exact:cmd`, `glob:pat`, `regex:pat`. First three reject chaining metacharacters (`;`, `|`, `&&`, `$(`, backtick); regex alone bypasses guard, use deliberately. `run_command` program+argv is synthesized and matched like bash. `git_read` supports fixed read-only git commands and needs only `--allow-tool git_read`. Any tool call or command not matched by an allow rule is denied immediately; there is no permission prompt.
Equivalent `rush.json`: `{"permissions":{"run":{"restrict":true,"allow_tools":["view"],"allow_bash":["git diff","glob:ls *"]}}}`. CLI lists union with config; `--restrict-run` forces restrict on. Global non-run `permissions.allowed_tools` is an earlier bypass: `bash` there approves all shell regardless, so leave it clear when patterns should govern. Applies only to noninteractive `rush run`, not TUI/web. Add restrict when appropriate without human authorization: narrows risk, unlike peak-hours bypass.

## Run completion, session liveness, and batches
The harness's foreground-call return or retained process/job handle completion establishes whether that specific `rush run` process exited; retain the handle and wait for that evidence. A CLI status snapshot, log/redirect contents, message finish, or a child's status is not a substitute. In particular, never infer physical process exit from `sessions why` saying `crashed`, `sessions locks` saying `offline`, or `sessions show` alone. Locks are held during turns and can be absent between turns; `why` and `show` are snapshots. Use `sessions watch <id>` to follow session activity; use `sessions why <id>` for combined session/batch evidence, `sessions jobs <id>` for owned jobs, and `rush batch show <root>` for a batch tree.

A top-level run can exit while other independent batch roots remain; resolve only the batch work in the task's related scope before an action that depends on it. Do not resume/relaunch, integrate, or commit this task until its process is confirmed exited and its relevant owned/related batch work is terminal. Pending, starting, running, and cancelling roots are held; `batch unknown` or an incomplete read is not terminal evidence. A held child question remains answerable via `inject_agent`; do not treat its pause as process exit or terminal work. Termination alone does not establish task acceptance.

`end_turn` ends an assistant turn, not necessarily the task; `between_turns` means a run loop is still waiting/continuing; `unknown` means the read did not establish state. None means terminal task completion. Verify the requested acceptance evidence after liveness is settled.

## Questions and safe resume
A top-level `ask_question` stop with `exit_reason: "awaiting_answer"` is deliberate. Read `.error` for the question/options and resume only after the actual process exit, using the same session and original supported role (`--role` is required): `rush run --role <original-role> --session <id> "<answer>"`. Answer from known context or pass a genuine operator decision back verbatim. Do not use `sessions inject` to resume this stopped top-level run. Sessions are bound to their creating checkout; resume there, or deliberately fork with `rush sessions fork <id> --cwd <path>` to continue elsewhere. If `ask_question` reports live own work instead of stopping, wait with `await_tasks` or finish the turn; do not issue a resume command.

A legacy child question returns a `SUB-AGENT QUESTION` result while its parent continues; resume that same child via `agent(resume_session_id="<full child session id>", prompt="<answer>")`. For a current held batch-child question, `inspect_agent` reports `awaiting_answer` and `held_question` identity (node, token, depth, sequence); answer the existing held generation via `inject_agent(child_session_id="<full child session id>", message="<answer>")`. Do not resume/re-delegate that held batch child as a new generation. Do not use top-level `sessions inject` to answer child questions. A paused/held child is not an exited top-level run.

## Context and recovery boundaries
Preserve session and task evidence when continuing after provider/model context compaction; follow only exposed behavior and controls. Model-context compaction summarizes history, unlike SQLite `VACUUM`. `rush sessions compact <session> [--role worker|smart|fast|reviewer]` defaults to `worker` and uses ordinary history summarization (`SummarizeNow`), not `Run`, a new leaf, replay, or a queue. Role resolution is the session override then the matching configured slot; unavailable roles, including custom roles, error without fallback. Use the correct project/config/data root. This is direct-provider-only; CLI backends are refused. Combined live or unreadable activity refuses immediately under mailbox/OS-lock coordination; busy work is not killed, bypassed, queued, or automatically resumed. A summary may exceed worker capacity; errors preserve original history, without a universal recovery guarantee. Ended external processes are not resurrected; no consumer-session mutation occurs. With no session, `rush sessions compact` remains database-only SQLite `VACUUM`; `--dry-run`, `--force`, and `--json` are DB-only and rejected with a session even when false; `--role` without a session is rejected. Database `--dry-run` may checkpoint WAL. Output truncation and `sessions truncate`/`reset` are not context compaction. See [docs/sessions-compact.md](docs/sessions-compact.md).

**Automatic recovery (direct Codex only):** On an ordinary `rush run`/resume, only an exact structured `context_length_exceeded` certified before any output (HTTP 400 or SSE `response.failed`) permits one silent-prefix summary and continuation in that same session. Partial, opaque, or uncertified output, transport errors, and NoReplay-fenced failures are never replayed. The summary uses only the captured matching worker session override/config (or covered per-call credentials); there is no silent role/provider fallback, and CLI workers are unsupported. Recovery preserves pinned context, the original user message, and the accepted tool-call/result tail, then continues with the original model, captured tools, and authority without re-executing accepted tools. Missing/unavailable workers, unknown or insufficient capacity, budget caps, or failed/cancelled summaries fail truthfully; history is not deleted before successful publication. There is one recovery attempt and continuation; a second overflow is terminal. Capacity reserve accounts for effective output allowance plus cache-inclusive occupancy; no task size, including task 371, is guaranteed to fit. This does not resurrect an already-exited process; an ordinary run/resume requires the matching installed release.

## Steering: `sessions inject`
Send new context to an existing run without killing/relaunching:
```
rush sessions inject <id> -m "also update the CHANGELOG"
rush sessions inject <id> -f ./notes/next-step.md
rush sessions inject <id> -m "stop — wrong approach" --interrupt
```
ID is launch `--session` (short hash okay). Default merge arrives next provider step without canceling current turn; `--interrupt` cancels current turn and restarts with message plus prior output. It persists as a normal user message visible in watch/last/web. If not running, persists for next run. Waiting between turns on job/delegation/retry counts as running (`running:true`, `between_turns:true`); no turn to cancel, message reaches next loop turn or next run. Cross-process via session DB; add `--json` for `{session_id,message_id,running,status}` and, between turns, `between_turns`/`driver_pid`.

## Repo defaults and model effort
`./.rush/system-prompts/default.md` auto-loads when no non-empty `--system-prompt` or `--system-prompt-file` content is provided; an explicitly empty prompt does not suppress the repo default. A non-empty explicit prompt or file takes precedence. Use repo-wide always-rules (scope, final message, no commit/push, tests, ambiguity). `rush models efforts [model]` lists/validates effort levels; `rush models bump <smart|fast|worker|reviewer> <up|down>` steps role effort (README.md `rush models` for details).

## When the lock is stuck
Don't `rm` lock (Windows OS handle prevents it). Use `rush sessions kill <id>` (kills PID/removes lock), `rush sessions kill <id> --wait 10s`, `rush sessions reset <id> --force` (also wipes history; refuses live work, cancel first), or `rush sessions reap` (all orphan locks). Windows kill uses `taskkill /F /T /PID` for whole `rush.exe`→`claude.cmd`→`node.exe` tree, waits for PID exit and retries lock removal.

## After the run finishes — you are responsible for verifying everything
Final text/JSON and worker reports are claims, not receipts. Inspect the actual diff, scope, acceptance evidence, and changed tests for non-vacuous regression value. Verification must follow caller/operator policy; do not mandate local execution. When CI-only verification is requested, run no local tests/build/vet/lint/typecheck, label the result CI-only, and state the exact CI commands without claiming they ran. Otherwise run only checks the caller authorized. Do not hand-fix unless asked or permitted. Report what actually changed and what was/wasn't verified.
Envelope: `.rush/stdin/<task>.out` first; `.warnings[]` `final_text is empty` can mean a fan-out without composed top-level reply, a tool_call without final text, or no tools/actionable output; inspect the specific warning, then use `git status` and `rush sessions last <id>` as needed. `sessions watch <id>` reports session activity but is not physical-process exit proof; `sessions why <id>` is an evidence snapshot.

## Time limits
`--timeout` defaults to `0` (no explicit deadline). Without it, Rush applies a default six-hour (6 h) TOTAL wall-clock cap, including active work and all waits (jobs, delegations, and other between-turn waits); progress does not reset this cap. A positive `--timeout` replaces the default cap. `RUSH_RUN_DEFAULT_HARD_TIMEOUT` overrides the default cap only. `--timeout-extends-on-progress` extends only the per-turn stream watchdog, not the total deadline. At a total deadline Rush attempts graceful cancellation; a final envelope is not guaranteed. If the process remains alive 60 seconds later, the hard backstop force-kills it (exit 124). `--idle-timeout` (default `15m`) is a separate quiet-period limit during a turn. It watches turns only; it does not bound between-turn waits. For recovery, inspect the reported timeout source and follow caller authorization and the safe-resume rules above; do not automatically raise `--timeout` or infer deadlock or its absence from a timeout.
